question:
In the figure, \(\angle EAB\) and \(\angle ABC\) are right angles, \(AB = 4,\) \(BC = 6,\) \(AE = 8,\) and \(\overline{AC}\) and \(\overline{BE}\) intersect at \(D.\) What is the difference between the areas of \(\triangle ADE\) and \(\triangle BDC?\)

[Figure 1](figures/2004_AMC_10A_Q09_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
The requested triangles remain when the same triangle \(ABD\) is removed from two right triangles whose areas we can calculate. Let \([XYZ]\) denote the area of triangle \(XYZ\).

The given right angles make \(AE\) and \(BC\) perpendicular to \(AB\). Using \(AB=4\) as the base gives
\[
[ABE]=\frac12\cdot4\cdot8=16,
\qquad
[ABC]=\frac12\cdot4\cdot6=12.
\]
Since \(D\) lies on both segments \(BE\) and \(AC\),
\[
[ABE]=[ABD]+[ADE],
\]
\[
[ABC]=[ABD]+[BDC].
\]
Subtracting cancels the common area \([ABD]\), so
\[
[ADE]-[BDC]=16-12=4.
\]
Thus triangle \(ADE\) is larger by \(\boxed{4}\) square units, choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
